facts: Volume is measured in cubic units: cm$^{3}$, m$^{3}$.
A cube has equal edges, so its volume is **edge $\times$ edge $\times$ edge**.
steps: Read the length, width and height (use the same unit).
Multiply length $\times$ width $\times$ height. If a dimension is missing, divide the volume by the product of the other two.
Write volume answers with cubic units and missing dimensions with length units.

workedExamples.question_text:
(a) A rectangular box is $7$ cm long, $5$ cm wide and $3$ cm high. Find its volume.
(b) A rectangular storeroom is $9$ m long, $5$ m wide and $4$ m high. Find its volume.
workedExamples.solution_text:
(a) One layer contains $7\times5=35$ cubic-centimetre units.
$35\times3=105$.
The volume is $105\text{ cm}^3$.
(b) $9\times5=45$ cubic-metre units in one layer.
$45\times4=180$.
The volume is $180\text{ m}^3$.

workedExamples.question_text: A cube has edges of $7$ cm. A student writes $7\times7=49\text{ cm}^2$ as its volume. Explain and correct the error.
workedExamples.solution_text:
$7\times7=49$ gives the number of cubic-centimetre units in one layer. There are $7$ layers.
$49\times7=343$.
The student left out the height and recorded area units. The volume is $343\text{ cm}^3$.

workedExamples.question_text: A rectangular box has dimensions $80$ mm, $7$ cm and $3$ cm. Find its volume in cubic centimetres.
workedExamples.solution_text:
Use centimetres for every dimension.
$80\text{ mm}=8\text{ cm}$.
$8\times7=56$.
$56\times3=168$.
The volume is $168\text{ cm}^3$.

workedExamples.question_text: A rectangular prism has volume $390\text{ cm}^3$. Its length is $13$ cm and its width is $5$ cm. Find its height and check the answer.
workedExamples.solution_text:
$13\times5=65$ cubic-centimetre units in one layer.
$390\div65=6$ layers.
The height is $6$ cm.
Check: $13\times5\times6=390\text{ cm}^3$.

development.question_text:
A rectangular planter is $6$ m long, $2$ m wide and $1$ m high.
Find its volume.

A box has a base $7$ cm by $5$ cm and height $4$ cm.
Find its volume.

A student gives $10\times3\times2=60\text{ cm}^2$ for a prism.
Correct the answer.
development.solution_text: The calculation is correct but volume needs cubic units. The answer is $60\text{ cm}^3$.

development.question_text:
A $4$ m by $3$ m by $2$ m prism is divided into $1\text{ m}^3$ cubes.
How many cubes fill it?
development.solution_text:
$4\times3\times2=24$
It is filled by $24$ cubes, so its volume is $24\text{ m}^3$.

mastery.question_text:
A rectangular prism has volume $144\text{ cm}^3$, length $8$ cm and width $3$ cm.
Find its height.

A cube has edge length $6$ cm.
A student says its volume is $6+6+6=18\text{ cm}^3$.
Correct the calculation and explain the error.
mastery.solution_text:
$6\times6\times6=216$
The volume is $216\text{ cm}^3$; the student added the dimensions instead of multiplying them.
